source_text: Nec te hoc putare, quia reatu voluntatis semina omnium hominum polluantur, sed tamen hanc iustitiam in Adae solius crimine non valere, ipsius unum esse peccatum, quod omnibus imputetur. Ad quod ego quid prius facere debeam nescio: rideamne, quod ineptiae exigunt singulares? Sed multorum perditio, quos decipitis, miserationem expectat et lacrimas. Serio ergo maerore conficiar? Sed argumentorum tuorum prodigia incutiunt, quamvis maesto animo, cachinnum.
pass_a_gloss: Nor that you think this, because by the guilt of will the seeds of all humans are polluted, but nevertheless that this justice does not avail in the crime of Adam alone, that his is the one sin which is imputed to all. To which I do not know what I ought first to do: shall I laugh, which singular ineptitudes demand? But the perdition of many whom you deceive expects pity and tears. Shall I therefore be afflicted with serious mourning? But the prodigies of your arguments strike a guffaw, although upon a mourning mind.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: You do not think the reproductive seed of all people is polluted by the guilt of an act of will; yet you claim this justice has no force in the case of Adam’s crime alone, and his is the one sin charged to everyone. I do not know how to respond first. Should I laugh, as your extraordinary absurdities demand? But the destruction of the many people you deceive calls for pity and tears. Should I therefore be overcome by earnest grief? Yet your monstrous arguments provoke laughter even in a sorrowful mind.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
